claim_boundary: These 24 assignments are full-paper analyst judgments anchored in captured D3 notes and text. They do not close the whole-corpus queue.

rows.title: Reconstruction of the Complete Vocal Tract Contour Through Acoustic to Articulatory Inversion Using Real-Time MRI Data
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper infers coordinated vocal-tract movement from acoustic evidence; it is about the physical source/filter relationship, not ordinary word recognition.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Infer the shape of the whole vocal tract from the sound a speaker produces. Mechanism: The acoustic sequence is mapped to contour coordinates; phonetic segmentation is tested as an auxiliary signal and RMSE/median geometric error measure reconstruction. Reported result: The paper reports 1.65 mm ABA and 1.69 mm AAT mean RMSE, compared with a 1.62 mm MRI pixel size. Boundary: The data are 2D MRI with 1.62 mm pixels and 8 mm slice thickness; acquisition and contour tracking introduce error. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: Bridging ASR and LLMs for Dysarthric Speech Recognition: Benchmarking Self-Supervised and Generative Approaches
rows.semantic_reasoning: The central comparison is how acoustic encoders and language-aware decoders map dysarthric speech to words; the clinical population is an important boundary, not the main mechanism.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Make transcription usable for dysarthric speech whose motor impairments distort phonemes, timing, and clarity. Mechanism: Acoustic representations produce candidates and an LLM uses context to select or repair sequences; WER is compared across TORGO and UASpeech. Reported result: The paper reports better Whisper results than CTC baselines and lower WER for LLM-assisted decoding in its experiments. Boundary: Cross-dataset generalization is poor, dysarthric data are limited, and not all encoder-decoder combinations were evaluated.

rows.title: Investigating the Reasoning Abilities of Large Language Models for Understanding Spoken Language in Interpersonal Interactions
rows.semantic_reasoning: The study tests whether language models use context and domain knowledge to interpret spoken questions; it concerns intended meaning rather than waveform recovery.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Classify whether a job-interview answer is under-explained, succinct, comprehensive, or over-explained. Mechanism: Prompt factors condition a four-class decision; macro-F1 compares performance across classes. Reported result: The paper reports selected macro-F1 results near 0.50 and 0.55 for its two tasks, with context and combined prompt factors sometimes helping. Boundary: The dataset focuses on military veterans and interview contexts; generalization across occupations, cultures, languages, and interaction styles is unresolved.

rows.title: Towards Better Disentanglement in Non-Autoregressive Zero-Shot Expressive Voice Conversion
rows.semantic_reasoning: The model separates multilingual content units from expressive voice controls so a new speaker/style can be produced without changing the requested content.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Transfer a target speaker's voice and expression while preserving source linguistic content and reducing source-style leakage. Mechanism: Content units encode linguistic material, style encoders represent speaker/emotion, and cross-attention injects local pitch into generated regions. Reported result: The paper reports improved emotion and speaker similarity and reduced source-style leakage versus its baselines. Boundary: The authors identify remaining intelligibility and cross-lingual challenges; this atlas did not run the model or inspect its demo independently.

rows.title: Location-Aware Target Speaker Extraction for Hearing Aids
rows.semantic_reasoning: The target is selected using direction of arrival for a hearing-aid microphone array; the decisive cue is spatial structure, not generic denoising.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Help a listener follow one person amid competing speakers, noise, and reverberation. Mechanism: Binaural time-frequency features are conditioned on direction so learned filtering emphasizes the target; SI-SDR and intelligibility measures are evaluated. Reported result: The paper reports about +9.93 dB SI-SDR and +0.208 absolute HASPI for FILM-exp in its stated 1,000-utterance setup. Boundary: The evaluation is scenario-specific; future work includes direction estimation and scenes with more than two speakers. Objective scores are not clinical outcomes.

rows.title: VoxAging: Continuously Tracking Speaker Aging with a Large-Scale Longitudinal Dataset in English and Mandarin
rows.semantic_reasoning: The longitudinal recordings ask how speaker verification changes as a person ages; time-varying identity is the phenomenon being measured.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Measure how a voice changes over years and how that changes speaker-verification decisions. Mechanism: Repeated observations allow verification scores and equal-error rates to be compared as the time gap grows, with age and gender analyses. Reported result: The paper reports declining verification performance and speaker similarity with increasing time span, with differences across age and gender groups. Boundary: The demographic and language composition is not universal; collection, labeling, and model execution were not independently audited here.

rows.title: Is it all about race? A Cross-examination of /s/ in a Multilingual Nigerian Context
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper measures /s/ variation across a multilingual Nigerian population and treats ethnicity, age, gender, and phonological context as boundaries on interpretation.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Identify which social and linguistic factors shape /s/ pronunciation in Nigerian English. Mechanism: Acoustic measurements operationalize frontness/backness and duration; statistical comparisons associate variation with linguistic and sociolinguistic factors. Reported result: The paper reports age and ethnicity effects among Igbo, Yoruba, and Hausa Nigerian English speakers, with limited gender differences in this analysis. Boundary: The result concerns this corpus and phoneme; acoustic measures should not be treated as direct proof of identity categories.

rows.title: Enabling the replicability of speech synthesis perceptual evaluations
rows.semantic_reasoning: The contribution is a reproducible perceptual-evaluation procedure; it belongs to the problem of what a listener score establishes and how to report it.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Make subjective speech-synthesis evaluations sufficiently specified for meaningful repetition and comparison. Mechanism: Separate the readable report from supplementary procedural data; distinguish reproducibility with the same inputs from replicability across new participants and data. Reported result: The contribution is a proposed platform and reporting structure intended to make evaluation choices inspectable. Boundary: Human subjective evaluations cannot simply be rerun with identical participants; adoption and future standards remain open, and the platform was not executed here.

rows.title: ashihara25_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper studies what discrete audio tokens preserve and how token predictability changes across domains; it is a representation question, not a claim of universal semantic units.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Understand what discrete audio tokens preserve when speech, music, and general audio are represented for language models. Mechanism: The study measures statistical structure and predictability of token sequences, then compares domain-specific codeword usage. Reported result: The paper reports similar statistical/predictable sequence patterns across domains but domain-dependent token usage. Boundary: The analysis supports representation observations, not a universal optimal token design or downstream task improvement.

rows.title: agrawal25b_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: The method finds bias phrases in cross-attention and merges them with ASR output, using task context to resolve otherwise difficult terms.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Recognize rare business words and out-of-vocabulary terms in contact-center ASR. Mechanism: Attention weights identify likely bias phrases; the method combines those candidates with the base transcription and uses an auxiliary attention loss. Reported result: The paper reports a 1.0% absolute WER reduction on LibriSpeech and improved OOV recognition on in-house contact-center data. Boundary: The in-house data are not independently available in this atlas, and future multilingual/low-resource extension remains open.

rows.title: agrawal25_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper probes whether speech-language models rely on label semantics and context when answering tasks; the conceptual issue is intended task meaning, not only transcription.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Make a speech-text LLM perform spoken-language-understanding tasks it did not see during task-specific training. Mechanism: The model maps speech and demonstrations to symbolic targets, then is evaluated in matched and mismatched task settings with zero/few-shot context. Reported result: The paper reports improved unseen-task performance over standard approaches in its three-task evaluation. Boundary: Fine-tuning used batch size one and the task/model/data setup is narrower than general spoken reasoning.

rows.title: abdullah25_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: Voice conversion is used as augmentation, but the paper's evaluated object is cross-domain dialect identification; the current question is whether dialect evidence survives changes in speaker realization.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Improve Arabic dialect identification when test speech comes from a different domain or speaker population. Mechanism: Converted speech changes speaker characteristics while preserving dialect-related content; controlled experiments compare conversion with ordinary augmentation. Reported result: The paper reports up to +34.07% cross-domain accuracy improvement and releases a model and evaluation dataset. Boundary: The result is specific to Arabic dialect identification and the released artifacts require separate access and execution checks.

rows.title: alip25_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: The three-stage system estimates acoustic structure, reduces full-band noise, and refines the spectrum; its boundary is enhancement quality versus faithful speech recovery.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Enhance multi-channel speech in low-SNR conditions by learning both spatial and spectral structure. Mechanism: Noisy multi-channel inputs produce speech-structure features that interact with spatial cues before later refinement stages. Reported result: The paper reports improvements over a reference method on LibriSpeech-based datasets. Boundary: The evidence is benchmark-bound and the summary does not establish performance in arbitrary rooms, languages, or devices.

rows.title: akinrintoyo25_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: The explicit filler-inclusion analysis makes preservation of disfluencies part of the target rather than treating them as transcription noise; the dementia population is the evaluation boundary.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Transcribe dementia speech while retaining filler words that may matter for clinical analysis and supportive interaction. Mechanism: Shorter training clips adapt the model to fragmented speech; transcripts are scored for word errors and filler detection. Reported result: The paper reports a medium model WER of 0.24 and stronger results than off-the-shelf models in its evaluation. Boundary: The dataset is 11.39 hours, some audio is mumbled or unintelligible, and diagnostic or clinical benefit is not established by ASR scores alone.

rows.title: biswas25_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: The method combines language prompts and code-mixed augmentation, so the core problem is switching language systems within speech rather than generic multilingual scaling.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Adapt Whisper to Hindi-English code-mixed speech with limited labeled data. Mechanism: Synthetic switches and language prompts expose the recognizer to transition patterns; MER and code-switch bigram accuracy evaluate transcription. Reported result: The paper reports a 31% relative improvement over pretrained Whisper without real in-domain data for fine-tuning. Boundary: The experiments focus on Hindi-English tutorial speech and Whisper large-v2; transfer to other language pairs is proposed, not established.

rows.title: giraldo25_interspeech
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper compares enhancement on multilingual crowdsourced speech and measures content retention and information loss across people; the evaluation target is human-useful recovery, not only a signal score.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Test whether speech-enhancement rankings survive demographic, language, and realistic data variation. Mechanism: Quality, intelligibility, word error, and phoneme error measures are compared across demographic and language conditions; samples with high WER are examined for information loss. Reported result: The paper reports performance variation across demographics/languages and warns that model rankings on VoiceBank-DEMAND do not transfer directly. Boundary: The authors still note benchmark simplification and possible metric overfitting; dataset diversity does not by itself prove universal fairness.

rows.title: Analysis of Avian Biphonic Vocalization Using Computational Modelling
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper models a dual avian sound source and upper vocal tract to explain how physical geometry produces biphonic spectral structure.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Explain how a bird can produce two simultaneous vocal components from a coupled sound source and vocal tract. Mechanism: A reconstructed syrinx and upper tract are represented in COMSOL; source placement and geometric parameters are changed, then simulated vocalizations are compared with recordings of real birds. Reported result: The paper reports experimentally validated biphonic simulations and systematic effects of tract geometry on resonance modulation and syllable bandwidth. Boundary: The model concerns avian vocalization rather than human speech; micro-CT reconstruction, source assumptions, and validation recordings constrain the result. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: AfriHuBERT: A self-supervised speech representation model for African languages
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper expands self-supervised pretraining across African languages so useful speech units can be learned where labeled data are scarce.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Provide reusable speech knowledge for African languages that have little labeled training data. Mechanism: Unlabeled audio is converted into masked prediction targets; the encoder learns from contextual speech patterns across languages and is then adapted for recognition and language-related tasks. Reported result: The paper reports a representation model expanded to 1,226 African languages and evaluates its transfer against multilingual baselines. Boundary: Language coverage does not mean equal data quality or equal downstream performance; the languages, hours, speaker balance, and task results determine the practical reach. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: Chain-of-Thought Training for Open E2E Spoken Dialogue Systems
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper adds intermediate reasoning supervision to an end-to-end spoken dialogue system, making conversational state part of the response decision.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Make a spoken dialogue system choose a useful response when the user's words, intent, and conversational state must be handled together. Mechanism: Speech is encoded into a shared representation, the model predicts intermediate dialogue reasoning, and a decoder produces the next response; ablations compare direct response training with the added supervision. Reported result: The paper reports improvements for open end-to-end spoken dialogue modeling from chain-of-thought training and evaluates the resulting response behavior. Boundary: Reasoning traces are supervision artifacts and do not prove faithful internal reasoning; task distribution, annotation quality, and evaluation subjectivity constrain the claim. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: Finding the Human Voice in AI: Insights on the Perception of AI-Voice Clones from Naturalness and Similarity Ratings
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper separates listener judgments of clone naturalness and target similarity and studies prosodic variation as a reason they diverge.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Determine whether a generated voice sounds like a person and whether listeners experience it as naturally spoken. Mechanism: Listeners hear natural and generated samples, rate distinct targets, and the analysis relates ratings to acoustic/prosodic differences rather than collapsing them into one number. Reported result: The paper reports that AI voice clones struggle with dynamic F0 variation and analyzes its relationship to naturalness and similarity ratings. Boundary: Listener population, prompts, voices, and rating protocol limit generalization; perceptual association does not establish that changing F0 alone fixes naturalness. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: Deep-Simplex Multichannel Speech Separation
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper addresses multichannel separation when the number of simultaneous speakers is not fixed, using mixture structure rather than a known source count.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Separate simultaneous speakers using multiple microphones without requiring a fixed number of speakers or an impractically large model. Mechanism: The model consumes multichannel mixtures, estimates source structure and spatial cues, and recursively extracts separated streams; experiments compare source-count and computational behavior. Reported result: The paper reports multichannel separation results with a deep-simplex approach designed for variable source conditions and compares it with established separators. Boundary: Performance depends on microphone geometry, room conditions, source count, and the reference metrics; synthetic mixtures may not represent real overlap. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: ATMM-SAGA: Alternating Training for Multi-Module with Score-Aware Gated Attention SASV system
rows.semantic_reasoning: The SASV system combines claimed-speaker evidence with anti-spoofing evidence because a voice match alone does not establish an authentic speaker.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Decide whether a claimed speaker is the person in a test utterance while resisting impostors and confusing acoustic conditions. Mechanism: Speaker and spoof-related representations are produced separately, gates weight evidence according to scores, and the final decision combines identity and authenticity signals; trials measure both acceptance and rejection errors. Reported result: The paper reports an alternating multi-module SASV system with score-aware gating and evaluates it on speaker-authentication trials. Boundary: Thresholds and spoof types determine operating behavior; benchmark attacks do not exhaust unseen synthesis or replay conditions. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: A Study of Speech Embedding Similarities Between Australian Aboriginal and High-Resource Languages
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper studies whether learned speech geometry relates Australian Aboriginal languages to high-resource languages, while testing the limits of interpreting similarity as transfer.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Understand whether speech representations preserve useful relationships for Australian Aboriginal languages despite their limited digital data. Mechanism: Audio from multiple languages is passed through a speech encoder; distances or similarity distributions are compared across language pairs and conditions, with downstream implications analyzed. Reported result: The paper reports comparative embedding similarities involving Australian Aboriginal and high-resource languages and discusses implications for underrepresented-language technology. Boundary: Similarity is not a language description or a guarantee of recognition transfer; data quantity, speaker coverage, and community context limit interpretation. No independent reproduction was performed.

rows.title: SMARTMOS: Modeling Subjective Audio Quality Evaluation for Real-Time Applications
rows.semantic_reasoning: The paper predicts subjective audio-quality judgments for real-time use, directly addressing the gap between a cheap proxy and what listeners actually report.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Estimate how people judge audio quality quickly enough for a real-time system without running a new listening test every time. Mechanism: Audio examples and human scores are used to train a predictor; its estimates are compared with held-out subjective ratings across conditions and computational constraints. Reported result: The paper reports a real-time subjective-quality model intended to approximate listening-test judgments more cheaply and quickly. Boundary: Human ratings, test conditions, and audio distortions define the target; a predictor can reproduce annotator bias and fail on unseen codecs or populations. No independent reproduction was performed.
